model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Give an agent the format-neutral context needed to construct, disclose and inspect impact and readiness reports derived from a typed dependency graph, without acquiring authority to approve, execute, remediate or deliver.
model.scope_statement: This deliverable is the bounded impact-and-readiness reporting surface of the WM-XCT-037 Dependency / Impact mixin. It covers five report kinds (analyze-impact, dependency-conflict, change-readiness, mitigation-reference, notification-content); the analysis frame each report must declare (scenario, bound snapshot, traversal paths, propagation rules, excluded edges); the mandatory confidence, completeness and evidence disclosures; the treatment of degraded graph conditions (contradictory evidence, stale assertions, unknown endpoints, cycles, alternative satisfiers, partial coverage); and the requirement that machine-readable and human-readable conclusions resolve to one evidence set. Typed edge assertion, graph storage, approval, execution, remediation, message delivery and audit-trail storage are adjacent surfaces that are referenced, never modelled here.
in_scope: The five report kinds and the minimum content core each must carry before it may be cited
Report instance identity, revision, release status, issuing agent and supersession of this model's own records
Declaration and freezing of the change scenario, its variants and its declared assumptions
Binding a report to an immutable, digest-corroborated graph snapshot and recording graph event time separately from observation and issue time
Traversal parameters: direction, edge-type filters, depth and fan-out bounds, and the versioned propagation rules that map edge types to impact classes
Replayable impact paths and the register of excluded edges with typed exclusion reasons
Evidence citation with generating activity, derivation source, responsible agent and observation time
Mandatory confidence, completeness and coverage disclosures attached to each conclusion and to the report as a whole
Disclosure of degraded graph conditions: contradictions, staleness, unresolvable endpoints, cut cycles, alternative satisfiers and partial coverage
Anchoring of machine-readable and human-readable renditions to one shared conclusion and evidence identifier set
The report's explicit declaration of what it does not authorise and which model or role owns each downstream act
out_of_scope: Typed dependency edge definition, edge assertion lifecycle and graph persistence, which belong to the adjacent dependency-graph surface of this mixin
Approval, authorisation, go/no-go decision and change-advisory procedure
Execution, deployment, rollback or any operational act on the analysed system
Remediation and mitigation execution or verification of remediation effectiveness
Transmission, addressing, routing or receipt tracking of notifications
Audit-trail storage, retention and evaluation of access or change records
Physical deletion, erasure and retention-period execution
Severity or risk scoring algorithms and their published scores
Human organisational readiness such as training, staffing and communications planning
Cost, effort and scheduling estimation for a change
Live simulation or what-if execution against a running environment

boundary_notes.neighbor: Adjacent dependency-graph assertion surface of WM-XCT-037
boundary_notes.distinction: That surface defines node and edge types, dependency strength and the lifecycle of an edge assertion. This surface consumes those typed edges by reference and adds only traversal filters, propagation mappings and reporting obligations; it defines no new edge semantics.

Impact analysis determines the extent to which a change would affect a system; the decision to permit the change is a separate configuration change control act. Readiness reports are inputs to that decision and never record an approval, an approver or a decision outcome.

A mitigation-reference report cites candidate remediations already published by their owning source, with applicability conditions. Selection, application, restart handling and verification of a remediation belong to the remediation model.

This surface drafts notification content and its handling marking for a stated recipient class. Addressing, transmission, delivery confirmation and read receipts are owned entirely by the delivery model; no function here sends anything.

The report's evidence register is a citation list scoped to one report revision. It is not an audit trail: recording, retaining, protecting and evaluating audit records is owned by the audit model, which this surface references and to which it emits required record content.

The graph snapshot that a report binds to is produced and owned by the inventory model, including its own completeness aggregate. This surface carries a resolvable snapshot reference and digest and restates the snapshot's declared completeness; it does not author or correct the inventory.

Severity, exploitability and business-criticality scores are carried into a report by reference with their scoring system named. This surface neither defines a scoring algorithm nor recomputes a score.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core model, Relationship class
sources.relevance: Normative model of a dependency relationship as a first-class element with from, to, relationshipType, completeness, startTime and endTime; grounds path steps, edge citation and temporal bounds on an asserted edge.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - RelationshipCompleteness vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines complete, incomplete and noAssertion as explicit completeness assertions on a relationship set; the normative basis for requiring a per-set completeness disclosure rather than an implied 'complete'.

sources.title: ECMA-424 CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification, 2nd edition (CycloneDX v1.7)
sources.relevance: Formal standardisation of the CycloneDX dependency graph, compositions and claim/attestation constructs; establishes that dependency graphs and their completeness assertions are standardised, exchangeable structures.

sources.title: OWASP CycloneDX Authoritative Guide to SBOM
sources.relevance: Documents the compositions aggregate values (complete, incomplete, incomplete_first_party_only, incomplete_third_party_only, unknown, not_specified) and the dependencies graph fields ref, dependsOn and provides; grounds scoped coverage disclosure and provided/virtual capabilities.

sources.title: Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) Version 2.0, OASIS Standard
sources.relevance: Separates document tracking (id, status draft/interim/final, revision_history, initial_release_date, current_release_date), product status (known_affected, known_not_affected, under_investigation, fixed), remediations and distribution/TLP; the closest normative analogue to a disclosed, revisioned impact report.

sources.title: Static Analysis Results Interchange Format (SARIF) Version 2.1.0, OASIS Standard
sources.relevance: Provides graph, node, edge, graphTraversal and edgeTraversal for replayable paths through a graph, result.baselineState (new, unchanged, updated, absent), result.rank, human-readable message alongside machine-readable properties, and resultProvenance with first/last detection times.

sources.title: STIX Version 2.1, OASIS Standard
sources.relevance: Defines a confidence property with named scales, the Opinion object (opinion, explanation, authors, object_refs) for retaining divergent assessments, and revoked / valid_from / valid_until / created / modified for staleness and withdrawal.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology, W3C Recommendation
sources.relevance: Entity, Activity, Agent with wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, used, wasAssociatedWith, startedAtTime and endedAtTime; the alignment target for evidence attribution and derivation in a report's evidence register.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.relevance: QualityMeasurement, Metric, Dimension and QualityAnnotation give a vocabulary for attaching completeness and confidence measurements to a dataset; used as an alignment for disclosure, not as a conformance claim (it is a Note, not a Recommendation).

sources.title: OpenVEX Specification
sources.relevance: Status values not_affected, affected, fixed, under_investigation with a mandatory justification or impact_statement for not_affected and a required action statement for affected; grounds the rule that a negative or reassuring conclusion must carry an explicit reason.

sources.title: Debian Policy Manual, Chapter 7: Declaring relationships between packages
sources.relevance: Depends, Pre-Depends, Recommends, Suggests, Enhances, Breaks, Conflicts, Provides and Replaces; alternatives expressed with the vertical bar; virtual packages; version relations; and explicit guidance that circular dependencies must be avoided and, where unavoidable, cut at a defined point.

sources.title: Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) Version 2.0 Standard Definitions and Usage Guidance
sources.organization: FIRST (Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams)
sources.relevance: TLP:RED, TLP:AMBER, TLP:AMBER+STRICT, TLP:GREEN and TLP:CLEAR with their sharing rules and document marking requirements; the handling vocabulary carried on report renditions and notification-content drafts.

sources.title: NIST Computer Security Resource Center Glossary - security impact analysis
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: Current entry, citing NIST SP 800-128, SP 800-137, SP 800-30 Rev. 1, SP 800-39 and SP 800-53 Rev. 5
sources.relevance: Defines impact analysis as the analysis conducted to determine the extent to which a change has affected a system - an analytical act distinct from configuration change control; the authority for separating report generation from approval and implementation.

bundles.name: Impact and Readiness Report Construction
bundles.description: How an impact or readiness report is framed, computed and disclosed: what kind of report it is, what analysis frame it declares, and what evidence and disclosure obligations it must satisfy before it may be cited.
bundles.rationale: Published dependency and advisory standards treat an assessment as a revisioned, attributable document whose conclusions are meaningless without a declared scope, a declared completeness and a declared basis. CSAF fixes tracking, status and revision history; SPDX fixes per-relationship completeness; SARIF fixes replayable graph traversal; PROV-O fixes attribution and derivation. Grouping these into one construction bundle keeps the report's frame inseparable from its conclusions.

layers.name: Report Instance Frame
layers.description: The citable identity of a report instance, its kind, revision and release status, and the mandatory content core each of the five report kinds must carry.

findings.name: Report Instance Identity, Kind and Release Status
findings.description: Establishes a report as a citable record independent of its storage or serialization: which identifier resolves it, which of the five kinds it declares, which revision and release status it carries, which agent issued it under whose delegated authority, and how it is superseded or revoked. The status of the report is deliberately distinct from the status of the change it describes.

questions.text: Which identifier makes this report instance citable and re-resolvable independently of its file name, storage collection or serialization format?
answer_data: authoritative master-system report identifier issued by the Dimension's report system of record
governed IRI where a registry already governs the report
fallback UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension
explicit statement that snapshot digest, title and issue date are not identifiers

questions.text: Which of the five report kinds does this instance declare, and may a single instance declare more than one kind?
answer_data: kind code from the closed set analyze-impact, dependency-conflict, change-readiness, mitigation-reference, notification-content
single-kind constraint or an explicit composite declaration rule
kind-specific mandatory content core reference

questions.text: What release status does the instance carry, and which status values permit downstream citation?
answer_data: release status value from draft, interim, final
citable-from-status rule
superseded and withdrawn markers held separately from release status

questions.text: Which agent issued this report, and under whose delegated authority was the issuance made?
answer_data: issuing agent reference
delegating role or organisational unit reference
explicit statement that issuing authority conveys no approval authority

questions.text: How is a report instance superseded or withdrawn, and what happens to existing citations of the superseded revision?
answer_data: monotonic revision number
supersedes and superseded-by pointers
withdrawal flag with reason code
rule that superseded content is retained and never rewritten

data_elements.name: Report identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the report record under the model's identity priority; stable across storage migration and never reused.

data_elements.name: Report kind code
data_elements.description: Closed-vocabulary code naming which of the five report kinds this instance is.

data_elements.name: Report revision
data_elements.description: Monotonically increasing integer revision of the report identifier; never renumbered.

data_elements.name: Release status
data_elements.description: Draft, interim or final; controls whether the revision may be cited outside the authoring role.

data_elements.name: Issuing agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent that issued the revision, resolved in the Dimension's identity model.

data_elements.name: Report issue time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset recording when the revision was issued, distinct from any graph or observation time.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Pointer from a revision to the revision it replaces.

data_elements.name: Withdrawal marker
data_elements.description: Marker that the issuer has withdrawn the revision's conclusions, with a reason code; content is retained.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity, kind, revision, status and issuing-agent values are header fields carried inside the report artifacts declared in dep-rpt-report-kind-contract. Minting a separate identity artifact would create two competing carriers of record for the same report and allow the header to drift from the conclusions it labels, so this finding contributes inline reference data only.

findings.name: Report Kinds and Their Mandatory Content Cores
findings.description: Defines the five report kinds and the minimum content each must carry to be citable: what an analyze-impact report enumerates, how a dependency-conflict report expresses incompatibility and alternatives without asserting a resolution, which readiness criteria a change-readiness report must evaluate or explicitly mark unevaluated, what a mitigation-reference report may state about a candidate mitigation, and what content and handling marking a notification-content draft carries given that this model never transmits it.

questions.text: What must an analyze-impact report contain before it may be cited as a basis for a change decision?
answer_data: reached-element set with per-element impact class
impact path set reference
excluded-edge register reference
confidence and completeness disclosure block
bound snapshot and propagation rule version

questions.text: How does a dependency-conflict report express incompatibility, alternative satisfiers and provided or virtual capabilities without asserting a resolution?
answer_data: conflict assertion with the two or more constraints in tension
version relation operators and ranges
alternative satisfier set with no selection
provided or virtual capability references
explicit no-resolution statement

questions.text: Which readiness criteria must a change-readiness report evaluate, and which may it only record as unevaluated?
answer_data: criterion identifier and its declared source
per-criterion verdict from met, unmet, unevaluated
reason for any unevaluated criterion
statement that the aggregate verdict is advisory input to an external decision

questions.text: What may a mitigation-reference report state about a candidate mitigation, and what must it leave to the remediation model?
answer_data: citation of the mitigation as published by its owning source
applicability conditions and affected element bindings
restart or precondition notes carried verbatim by reference
explicit exclusion of selection, application and effectiveness verification

questions.text: What content and handling marking must a notification-content draft carry, given that this model performs no transmission?
answer_data: recipient class rather than individual addressees
handling marking such as a TLP label
conclusions cleared for that audience with their anchors
statement naming the delivery model that owns transmission

data_elements.name: Content core reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the mandatory content checklist for the declared report kind.

data_elements.name: Conflict assertion
data_elements.description: Statement that two or more dependency constraints cannot be satisfied together, naming each constraint and its version relation.

data_elements.name: Alternative satisfier set
data_elements.description: Set of elements any one of which satisfies a requirement, including virtual or provided capabilities; reported without selection.

data_elements.name: Readiness criterion verdict
data_elements.description: One criterion with its verdict of met, unmet or unevaluated, its evidence citation and its confidence.

data_elements.name: Mitigation reference
data_elements.description: Citation of an externally owned candidate mitigation with its applicability conditions and affected element bindings.

data_elements.name: Recipient class
data_elements.description: Named audience class for a notification-content draft; never an individual address or transport endpoint.

data_elements.name: Handling marking
data_elements.description: Sharing-restriction label applied to a report or draft, such as a TLP 2.0 label, inherited from the most restrictive incorporated evidence item.

artifacts.name: Analyze-Impact Report
artifacts.description: Issued report enumerating the elements reached downstream of a declared scenario over a bound snapshot, with per-element impact class, path citations and a disclosure block. It states impact, never permission to proceed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system report identifier plus integer revision; the bound snapshot digest, scenario identifier and issue date are attributes, never identifiers.

artifacts.name: Dependency-Conflict Report
artifacts.description: Report of constraint incompatibilities discovered over the bound snapshot: version-range violations, mutually exclusive requirements, breakage relations and the alternative or virtual satisfiers available. It reports the conflict set and does not assert a resolution.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system report identifier plus integer revision; each conflict carries its own stable conflict identifier within the revision.

artifacts.name: Change-Readiness Report
artifacts.description: Per-criterion statement of whether the technical prerequisites for a declared scenario are met, unmet or unevaluated, each with evidence citation and confidence. It is an input to a decision owned by the change approval model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system report identifier plus integer revision; criterion verdicts are addressed by criterion identifier within the revision.

artifacts.name: Mitigation-Reference Report
artifacts.description: Reference list of candidate mitigations or workarounds already published by their owning sources, bound to impacted elements with applicability conditions. It carries citations, never an instruction to apply.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system report identifier plus integer revision; each entry retains the external identifier issued by the mitigation's owning source.

artifacts.name: Notification-Content Draft
artifacts.description: Drafted notification body addressed to a named recipient class, carrying a handling marking and only those conclusions cleared for that audience, each anchored to the machine-readable rendition. Drafting only; no transmission occurs in this model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master-system report identifier plus integer revision plus recipient-class discriminator; no transport message identifier is minted here.

layers.name: Analysis Frame
layers.description: The declared, frozen inputs that make a reported conclusion reproducible: the change scenario, the bound graph snapshot with its temporal semantics, and the traversal and propagation parameters together with the excluded-edge register.

findings.name: Change Scenario and Subject Declaration
findings.description: Declares the perturbation being analysed: the subject elements, the proposed action, the variants that must be reported alongside the primary scenario, the assumptions treated as preconditions rather than findings, and how a scenario is re-identified when the same change is re-analysed against a later snapshot.

questions.text: What subject elements and proposed action define this scenario, and how is a multi-part scenario bounded?
answer_data: subject element references resolved in the host model
proposed action code such as add, upgrade, downgrade, remove, replace, deprecate or unavailability
bounding rule for grouping several actions into one scenario

questions.text: Which scenario variants must be reported alongside the primary scenario, and how are they distinguished from it?
answer_data: variant identifier and label such as do-nothing, rollback or alternative substitution
primary-variant marker
per-variant conclusion set kept separately addressable

questions.text: Which assumptions are declared as scenario preconditions rather than reported as findings?
answer_data: declared assumption statement
assumption source and whether it was verified or asserted
effect on conclusions if the assumption fails

questions.text: How is a scenario re-identified when the same proposed change is re-analysed against a later snapshot?
answer_data: stable scenario identifier independent of snapshot
rule that a new snapshot produces a new report revision, not a new scenario
comparison pointer to the prior report revision

data_elements.name: Scenario identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of the declared change scenario, independent of any snapshot or report revision.

data_elements.name: Subject element reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an element in the host subject model that the scenario acts upon.

data_elements.name: Proposed action code
data_elements.description: Closed-vocabulary code describing the perturbation applied to the subject elements.

data_elements.name: Scenario variant
data_elements.description: A named alternative framing of the same change whose conclusions are reported separately from the primary variant.

data_elements.name: Declared assumption
data_elements.description: A precondition taken as given for the analysis, with its source and the stated consequence of its failure.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A scenario is the report's declared input frame rather than a separately issued deliverable. It is carried as reference data inside every report artifact that depends on it so that a report and the scenario it analysed cannot be separated, re-dated or re-bound independently; issuing it as its own artifact would permit exactly that drift.

findings.name: Graph Snapshot Binding and Temporal Validity
findings.description: Every report binds to one immutable, digest-corroborated snapshot of the dependency graph owned by an external source of record, and records graph event time, observation or ingestion time and report issue time as separate values. Also fixes the report's validity horizon, what invalidates it earlier, and how the snapshot's own declared coverage limits are restated.

questions.text: To which snapshot of the dependency graph is this report bound, and how is that binding kept verifiable after the graph has moved on?
answer_data: resolvable snapshot reference in the owning source of record
content digest of the snapshot
identifier of the snapshot-producing activity and agent

questions.text: How are graph event time, observation or ingestion time and report issue time recorded when they differ?
answer_data: graph event time when the dependency fact became true
observation or ingestion time when the snapshot captured it
report issue time
rule forbidding overwriting an observation time with a later ingestion time

questions.text: For how long does this report assert validity, and what invalidates it before that horizon?
answer_data: validity-until value
invalidating events such as snapshot supersession, propagation rule version change or withdrawal of a cited evidence item
resulting status transition of the report

questions.text: Which model owns the snapshot itself, and what may this report legitimately record about it?
answer_data: owning source-of-record model reference
permitted local fields limited to reference, digest, times and restated completeness
explicit prohibition on authoring or correcting inventory content here

questions.text: How does the report restate the snapshot's own declared coverage so that a reader does not mistake snapshot gaps for analysis gaps?
answer_data: snapshot-level completeness aggregate carried verbatim
attribution of each gap to snapshot origin or to traversal
statement that a no-assertion snapshot caps the report's own completeness claim

data_elements.name: Snapshot reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the graph snapshot in its owning source of record.

data_elements.name: Snapshot digest
data_elements.description: Content digest corroborating that the snapshot read is the snapshot cited; never used as an identifier.

data_elements.name: Graph event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and offset for when the underlying dependency fact became true, where known.

data_elements.name: Snapshot observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and offset for when the snapshot captured or ingested the graph state.

data_elements.name: Validity horizon
data_elements.description: Time after which the report's conclusions are not asserted to hold without re-analysis.

data_elements.name: Restated snapshot completeness
data_elements.description: The snapshot's own completeness aggregate, carried verbatim so that snapshot gaps are attributable to the snapshot.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The snapshot is authored and owned by an external inventory or graph source of record. Materialising a snapshot artifact here would duplicate that model's deliverable and invite divergence between two copies of the same state, so this finding carries only a resolvable reference, a corroborating digest, the separated time values and the restated coverage claim.

findings.name: Impact Paths, Propagation Rules and Excluded Edges
findings.description: How downstream impact is actually derived and made replayable: traversal direction, edge-type filters and depth or fan-out bounds; the versioned propagation rules mapping each traversed edge type to an impact class; the representation of an individual path as ordered edge steps; the register of edges not traversed with typed exclusion reasons; and how dependency strength distinctions affect propagation.

questions.text: Which traversal direction, edge-type filters and depth or fan-out bounds produced the reported impact set?
answer_data: direction of traversal relative to the subject
included edge-type filter list
maximum depth and fan-out bounds and whether either was reached

questions.text: Which propagation rule mapped each traversed edge type to an impact class, and where is that rule set versioned?
answer_data: propagation rule set reference and version
per-edge-type mapping to impact class
register location where rule versions are published

questions.text: Which edges were excluded from traversal, and was each exclusion a policy choice, a traversal bound or a data gap?
answer_data: excluded edge reference
exclusion reason code distinguishing policy, bound and gap
stated effect of the exclusion on the affected conclusions

questions.text: How is an individual impact path represented so that a reader can replay it edge by edge?
answer_data: ordered edge steps with source and target node identifiers
edge type and applied propagation rule at each step
step message explaining the transition
path identifier stable within the revision

questions.text: How are absolute, recommended and optional dependency strengths reflected in propagation weight and in the reported impact class?
answer_data: dependency strength code consumed from the graph surface
weighting or downgrade rule per strength
rule for optional edges that are traversed but reported at reduced impact

data_elements.name: Traversal direction
data_elements.description: Whether the traversal followed dependents, dependencies or both from the subject elements.

data_elements.name: Edge-type filter
data_elements.description: The set of edge types admitted into the traversal, consumed by reference from the graph surface.

data_elements.name: Depth or fan-out bound
data_elements.description: Configured traversal limit and a marker recording whether the limit was actually reached.

data_elements.name: Propagation rule set version
data_elements.description: Versioned reference to the rule set mapping edge types and strengths to impact classes.

data_elements.name: Impact path
data_elements.description: An ordered sequence of edge steps from a subject element to a reached element.

data_elements.name: Path edge step
data_elements.description: One traversal step recording edge identifier, source and target node, edge type, applied rule and an explanatory message.

data_elements.name: Excluded edge entry
data_elements.description: An edge that was not traversed, with its reason code and stated effect on conclusions.

data_elements.name: Dependency strength
data_elements.description: Strength class of a traversed edge, such as absolute, recommended, suggested or enhancing, consumed from the graph surface.

data_elements.name: Impact class
data_elements.description: The class of impact asserted for a reached element under the applied propagation rule.

artifacts.name: Impact Path Set
artifacts.description: Replayable traversal record for one report revision: every reported path as ordered edge steps with source and target node identifiers, edge type and the propagation rule applied at each step.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Addressed by owning report identifier and revision plus a path identifier unique within that revision; a content digest corroborates integrity only.

artifacts.name: Excluded-Edge Register
artifacts.description: Register of edges deliberately or unavoidably left untraversed, each with a reason code distinguishing policy exclusion, traversal bound and data gap, plus the effect of the exclusion on the conclusions it touches.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Addressed by owning report identifier and revision plus the excluded edge's identifier from the graph surface.

layers.name: Evidence and Disclosure
layers.description: What a conclusion must cite and what it must admit: the evidence register with provenance and attribution, and the mandatory confidence, completeness and coverage disclosures that qualify every conclusion.

findings.name: Evidence Items, Attribution and Derivation
findings.description: Each conclusion cites evidence items; each evidence item records the activity that generated it, the prior entity it was derived from, the agent responsible for it and when it was observed, so a conclusion can be re-derived or falsified. Distinguishes observed from asserted evidence, handles issuer withdrawal, and keeps the register distinct from the Dimension's audit trail.

questions.text: Which evidence items support each reported conclusion, and how is that citation expressed as a resolvable link rather than restated prose?
answer_data: conclusion anchor identifier

resolvable pointer to the evidence in its owning source
prohibition on citation by array index or line number

questions.text: Which activity generated each evidence item, from which prior entity was it derived, and to which agent is it attributed?
answer_data: generating activity identifier with start and end times
derived-from entity reference
responsible agent reference
alignment terms from a provenance vocabulary

questions.text: How is evidence observed by the report generator distinguished from evidence asserted by a third party?
answer_data: evidence kind code separating observation, assertion and inference
asserting party reference for third-party assertions
rule that an inference must cite the observations it rests on

questions.text: What must be recorded when a cited evidence item is later withdrawn or revoked by its issuer?
answer_data: evidence withdrawal marker with time and issuer

questions.text: How is the report's evidence register kept distinct from the adopting Dimension's audit trail?
answer_data: scope statement limiting the register to one report revision
reference to the audit model that owns event records
list of record content this model must emit to that audit model
explicit disclaimer of audit storage, retention and evaluation

data_elements.name: Evidence item identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a cited evidence item within the report revision, resolvable to its owning source.

data_elements.name: Evidence kind
data_elements.description: Whether the item is a direct observation, a third-party assertion or an inference drawn from other items.

data_elements.name: Generating activity
data_elements.description: The activity that produced the evidence item, with its start and end times.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference

data_elements.name: Responsible agent

data_elements.name: Evidence withdrawal marker

data_elements.name: Conclusion anchor
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of a single reported conclusion, used by both renditions and by every evidence citation.

artifacts.name: Report Evidence Register
artifacts.description: Citation register for one report revision listing each evidence item with its generating activity, derivation source, responsible agent and observation time, and the conclusion anchors it supports. It is a citation list scoped to the report, not the Dimension's audit trail.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Addressed by owning report identifier and revision; each entry retains the identifier issued by the evidence item's owning source.

findings.name: Confidence, Completeness and Coverage Disclosure
findings.description: The mandatory disclosures attached to each conclusion and to the report as a whole: a confidence value expressed on a named scale, a completeness assertion for each traversed relationship set drawn from complete, incomplete or explicit no-assertion, the fraction of the in-scope graph actually reached with a characterisation of what was not, and the method by which each was derived. Fixes the minimum disclosure set that gates release from draft.
