data_elements.name: Confidence scale reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the named scale definition, without which a confidence value is not interoperable.

data_elements.name: Completeness assertion
data_elements.description: Assertion of complete, incomplete or no-assertion for a named relationship set or scope.

data_elements.name: Coverage measurement
data_elements.description: Measured proportion of the in-scope graph actually traversed, with the metric definition it was measured against.

data_elements.name: Unreached region characterisation
data_elements.description: Description of the territory not traversed and why, so that unreached is not read as unaffected.

data_elements.name: Disclosure method reference
data_elements.description: Versioned reference to the method used to derive confidence, completeness and coverage values.

data_elements.name: Minimum disclosure set reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the Dimension-published list of disclosures that must be present before release from draft.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Disclosures are qualifiers that must travel attached to the specific conclusion or scope they qualify. Separating them into a standalone artifact would allow a conclusion to be quoted without its confidence, completeness and coverage caveats, which is the precise failure mode this finding exists to prevent, so they are declared as inline fields on the report artifacts and their conclusion anchors.

bundles.name: Report Integrity, Degradation and Handoff
bundles.description: How a report stays honest when the graph or its evidence is not clean, and how its conclusions are presented and handed on without acquiring authority the model does not have.
bundles.rationale: Real dependency graphs contain contradictions, expired assertions, unresolvable endpoints, cycles and choice points, and are almost never fully known. Every consulted standard provides an explicit construct for admitting this - SPDX no-assertion, CycloneDX unknown aggregates, CSAF and OpenVEX under-investigation, STIX revocation and validity windows, Debian cycle-cutting guidance. This bundle turns those constructs into obligations, and pairs them with the equally load-bearing rule that a report is an analytical instrument distinct from configuration change control.

layers.name: Degraded Graph and Contested Evidence
layers.description: Required behaviour when the graph or its evidence is contradictory, stale, unresolvable, cyclic, ambiguous or only partly known.

findings.name: Degraded Graph Conditions and Contested Evidence
findings.description: How contradictory assertions, stale assertions, unresolvable endpoints, cycles, alternative satisfiers and partial coverage are detected, recorded and disclosed. The governing rule is that degradation is reported rather than silently resolved: both sides of a contradiction are retained, a cut cycle is disclosed with its cut point, an unknown endpoint is marked rather than dropped, and a choice point is presented without selection.

questions.text: How are two contradictory assertions about the same edge reported without silently choosing a winner?
answer_data: contradiction record holding both assertions with their sources and assertion times
optional preferred reading with an explicit stated rationale
rule retaining the non-preferred assertion
mandatory confidence downgrade for dependent conclusions

questions.text: At what point is an assertion treated as stale, and what must the report say when it has to rely on one?
answer_data: declared staleness threshold or validity-until value from the assertion
stale marker with the age at time of use
statement of the conclusions that depend on stale input
required completeness or confidence downgrade

questions.text: How is an edge whose target cannot be resolved reported, and how does it affect the conclusions downstream of it?
answer_data: unknown-endpoint marker retaining the unresolved reference as given
reason such as missing record, ambiguous identifier or out-of-scope namespace
truncation note on every path that terminates at the unknown endpoint
effect on the coverage measurement

questions.text: How are cycles detected, cut and disclosed so that the reported path set stays finite without hiding the cycle?
answer_data: cycle record listing the participating nodes and edges
declared and versioned cut rule with the chosen cut point
statement that the cut is a reporting device and not an assertion about the real graph
effect on impact classes computed across the cycle

questions.text: When several alternative satisfiers exist for one requirement, how are they reported without asserting a selection?
answer_data: alternative satisfier set with each option's identifier
per-option impact consequence where computed
explicit no-selection statement
identification of the model or role that owns selection

data_elements.name: Contradiction record
data_elements.description: Two or more mutually inconsistent assertions about the same edge or element, retained together with their sources and assertion times.

data_elements.name: Staleness threshold
data_elements.description: Declared age or validity boundary past which an assertion is marked stale for reporting purposes.

data_elements.name: Stale assertion marker
data_elements.description: Marker on an input assertion that it exceeded the staleness threshold at the time it was used.

data_elements.name: Unknown endpoint marker
data_elements.description: Marker for an edge target that could not be resolved, retaining the unresolved reference and the reason.

data_elements.name: Cycle record
data_elements.description: Detected cycle with participating nodes and edges, the versioned cut rule applied and the chosen cut point.

data_elements.name: Partial coverage marker
data_elements.description: Marker that the traversal covered only part of the in-scope graph, bound to the region and cause.

data_elements.name: Degradation effect note
data_elements.description: Statement of how a specific degraded condition changes the reading of the conclusions it touches.

artifacts.name: Degradation and Known-Unknowns Register
artifacts.description: Register of every degraded condition encountered while producing one report revision: contradictions with both assertions retained, stale assertions, unresolvable endpoints, cut cycles, alternative satisfier sets and partial-coverage regions, each with its effect on the affected conclusions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Addressed by owning report identifier and revision plus a condition identifier unique within that revision; each entry retains the source identifier of the assertion or element it concerns.

layers.name: Rendition and Handoff
layers.description: How one report revision is presented in machine-readable and human-readable form against a single evidence set, and how it declares the limits of its own authority.

findings.name: Dual Rendition Traceability and Non-Authorising Handoff
findings.description: The machine-readable and human-readable renditions of one report revision must resolve to the same conclusion anchors and the same evidence register, and every rendition must carry an explicit declaration of the acts it does not perform together with the model or role that owns each of those acts. Also covers who may read each rendition and how a rendition is corrected without creating a second conclusion of record.

questions.text: How does a sentence in the human-readable rendition resolve to the same conclusion anchor and evidence citations as the machine-readable rendition?
answer_data: conclusion anchor identifier embedded in both renditions
evidence identifiers referenced identically in both
rule that a human-readable claim without an anchor is not a conclusion of record

questions.text: What must be true before two renditions of one report revision may be published as equivalent?
answer_data: equivalence attestation naming both renditions and the attesting role
check that every machine conclusion has an anchored human counterpart or a declared omission
check that no non-droppable disclosure was lost
shared revision digest chain

questions.text: Which downstream acts does this report explicitly not perform, and which model or role is named as owning each of them?
answer_data: enumerated non-performed acts covering approval, execution, remediation, delivery and audit storage
named owning model or role for each act
statement that no field in the report constitutes a decision, dispatch or completion record

questions.text: Who may read each rendition, and how does the report's handling marking constrain onward sharing?
answer_data: read scope per rendition
handling marking inherited from the most restrictive incorporated evidence
marking placement requirements on the rendition itself
named access model that executes grants and revocations

questions.text: How is a rendition regenerated or corrected without creating a second conclusion of record?
answer_data: rule that renditions share the revision number of the report they render
regeneration permitted only while the digest chain resolves to the same revision
content correction forcing a new revision and a new equivalence attestation

data_elements.name: Rendition identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one rendition, composed of the report identifier, its revision and a rendition discriminator.

data_elements.name: Rendition form
data_elements.description: Whether the rendition is the machine-readable carrier or a human-readable presentation, stated without naming a file format.

data_elements.name: Rendition equivalence attestation
data_elements.description: Attestation by a named role that two renditions of one revision carry the same conclusions, anchors and non-droppable disclosures.

data_elements.name: Non-authorising declaration
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of the acts the report does not perform, carried on every rendition.

data_elements.name: Downstream act owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference naming the model or role that owns each non-performed downstream act.

data_elements.name: Revision digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical form of the revision, binding both renditions to the same content.

artifacts.name: Machine-Readable Rendition
artifacts.description: The normative carrier of one report revision's conclusion anchors, evidence citations, path references and disclosure block, expressed in a structured form for programmatic consumption.
media_or_form: structured serialization independent of any particular encoding
artifacts.identity_strategy: Report identifier plus revision plus a machine-rendition discriminator; validity requires that its digest resolve to the revision's canonical form.

artifacts.name: Human-Readable Rendition
artifacts.description: Narrative or tabular presentation of the same revision in which every asserted conclusion carries the anchor of the machine-readable conclusion it restates, together with the handling marking and the non-authorising declaration.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Report identifier plus revision plus a human-rendition discriminator and, where applicable, a language variant tag; shares the revision digest of its machine counterpart.

functions.name: Bind report to graph snapshot
functions.description: Fix the immutable graph snapshot a report will be computed against, recording its resolvable reference, digest, observation time and restated completeness.
inputs: snapshot reference in the owning source of record
snapshot completeness aggregate as declared by its owner
outputs: snapshot binding record attached to a draft report instance
restated snapshot completeness carried into the disclosure block
preconditions: the snapshot is retrievable and its digest verifies
the owning source-of-record model is identified
effects: The report is bound to exactly one snapshot for the remainder of its revision; a different snapshot requires a new revision.
No change is made to the snapshot or to the inventory that owns it.

functions.name: Declare and freeze change scenario
functions.description: Record the subject elements, proposed action, variants and declared assumptions, then freeze them so conclusions cannot be reattributed to a different scenario.
outputs: frozen scenario declaration attached to the draft report instance
preconditions: subject elements resolve in the host subject model
a stable scenario identifier is available or can be minted
effects: Scenario content becomes immutable for the revision; amendment requires a new revision.
No change is proposed, scheduled or requested in any external system.

functions.name: Traverse impact paths
functions.description: Traverse the bound snapshot from the scenario subjects under a versioned propagation rule set, producing the reached-element set, the replayable path set and the excluded-edge register.
inputs: traversal direction, edge-type filter and depth or fan-out bounds
outputs: reached-element set with per-element impact class
impact path set of ordered edge steps
excluded-edge register with typed reason codes
preconditions: snapshot binding and scenario are frozen
the named propagation rule set version is published and resolvable
effects: Produces derived analysis content within the draft revision only.
Records every bound that was reached, so a truncated traversal cannot be mistaken for an exhausted one.

functions.name: Detect and record degraded conditions
functions.description: Identify contradictions, stale assertions, unresolvable endpoints, cycles, alternative satisfiers and partial-coverage regions encountered during traversal, and record each with its effect on affected conclusions.
inputs: traversal input assertions with their sources and assertion times
preconditions: traversal has produced a path set
staleness threshold and cut rule versions are declared
effects: Both sides of each contradiction are retained; no assertion is deleted or overwritten by this function.
Cycle cuts are recorded as reporting devices and never written back to the graph.

functions.name: Compute confidence, completeness and coverage disclosures
functions.description: Derive and attach the disclosure block: per-set completeness assertions, coverage measurement, and confidence values expressed on a named scale, capped by degradation and evidence conditions.
inputs: named confidence scale definition and disclosure method version
outputs: disclosure block attached to the report and to each conclusion anchor
preconditions: traversal, degradation detection and evidence citation have completed
the confidence scale and disclosure method are published and versioned
effects: Confidence is capped where completeness is incomplete or no-assertion, or where cited evidence is stale or withdrawn.
Absence of a computed value is recorded as an explicit no-assertion rather than defaulting to complete.

functions.name: Compose report instance of a declared kind
functions.description: Assemble a report revision of one declared kind from the frozen frame, path set, exclusion and degradation registers, evidence register and disclosure block, and open it in draft status.
inputs: path set, excluded-edge register and degradation register
outputs: draft report revision with a minted identifier and revision number
preconditions: all referenced components exist and belong to the same revision
the kind's mandatory content core is satisfiable from the available components
effects: Creates an immutable draft revision under the model's identity priority.
Confers no approval, dispatches no notification and asserts no operational completion.

functions.name: Validate report against the disclosure contract
functions.description: Check a report revision against the published minimum disclosure set and the confidence-consistency rules, and return a conformance verdict with the specific deficiencies found.
outputs: conformance verdict with pass or fail and an itemised deficiency list
preconditions: the report revision is complete enough to evaluate
the minimum disclosure set is published and versioned
effects: Produces a verdict record only; it does not block, publish, quarantine or remediate anything.
Enforcement of the verdict, including any gate on status change, is executed by the adopting Dimension's governance process, not by this function.

functions.name: Produce anchored renditions
functions.description: Generate the machine-readable and human-readable renditions of one report revision, anchored to the same conclusion identifiers and evidence citations, and record an equivalence attestation.
preconditions: the revision has passed the disclosure-contract check
a handling marking has been determined from the incorporated evidence
effects: Both renditions share the revision digest; a rendition whose digest chain breaks is marked unusable rather than silently regenerated.
Renditions are produced but not transmitted, published to an audience or distributed by this function.

functions.name: Supersede a report revision
functions.description: Issue a superseding revision of an existing report and mark the prior revision superseded, preserving its content and citation resolvability.
inputs: new frozen frame and recomputed components
outputs: new revision with a supersedes pointer
superseded-by pointer written on the prior revision
preconditions: the prior revision exists and is not hard-deleted
the new revision satisfies the minimum disclosure set
effects: The prior revision's content is never rewritten; only its status pointer is updated.
Existing citations of the prior revision continue to resolve and return the supersession pointer.

composition.target: Host subject model adopting the WM-XCT-037 mixin
composition.purpose: The reporting surface attaches to a host model that supplies the subject entities, their identifiers and their read scopes. This surface never defines the subject entities it reports on.

composition.target: Adjacent dependency-graph assertion surface of WM-XCT-037 (typed edges, strengths, edge lifecycle)
composition.purpose: Reports consume typed edges, dependency strengths and edge assertion metadata from that surface and add only traversal filters, propagation mappings and reporting obligations. Edge typing and assertion lifecycle are not restated here.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension component or asset inventory model (snapshot source of record)
composition.purpose: Supplies the immutable graph snapshot a report binds to, together with the snapshot's own completeness aggregate. This surface carries only a resolvable reference, a corroborating digest, separated time values and the restated completeness.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension change approval / change enablement model
composition.purpose: Receives readiness and impact reports as inputs and owns the decision to permit a change, the approving authority and the decision record. No approval field, approver or outcome is stored here.
Receives the issuance, supersession, tombstone and disclosure-recomputation records this surface is required to emit, and owns their storage, protection, retention and evaluation.
Owns retention periods, legal holds and physical erasure for report records. This surface owns only the tombstone contract and the requirement that a disposition be recorded.
Owns selection, application, restart handling and verification of mitigations. A mitigation-reference report carries citations and applicability conditions into this model and stops there.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension notification delivery / messaging transport model
composition.purpose: Owns addressing, transmission, delivery confirmation and receipt tracking for notification-content drafts produced here. No transport identifier, endpoint or delivery state is modelled in this surface.
Owns scoring algorithms and published severity values. Scores enter a report by reference with their scoring system named and are never recomputed here.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension access control and identity model
composition.purpose: Executes read-scope grants, revocations and emergency time-boxed access for report renditions. This surface states the default rule and the exceptions but performs no grant.

Alignment target for evidence attribution and derivation using Entity, Activity, Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom and wasAttributedTo. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed without recorded mapping evidence.

composition.target: SPDX 3.0.1 Relationship class and RelationshipCompleteness vocabulary
composition.purpose: Alignment target for edge citation and for per-relationship completeness assertions of complete, incomplete and no-assertion.

composition.target: ECMA-424 CycloneDX Bill of Materials Specification (compositions and dependency graph)
composition.purpose: Alignment target for scoped coverage aggregates and for dependency graph edges including provided or virtual capabilities. Granularity differences with SPDX completeness are recorded as a conflict.

composition.target: OASIS CSAF 2.0 and the OpenVEX Specification
composition.purpose: Alignment targets for revisioned advisory tracking, under-investigation status, and the requirement that a reassuring conclusion carry an explicit justification or impact statement.

composition.target: OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 graph, graphTraversal and edgeTraversal objects
composition.purpose: Alignment target for representing a replayable path through a graph and for pairing a human-readable message with machine-readable result properties.

composition.target: OASIS STIX 2.1 confidence, Opinion, revoked and validity properties
composition.purpose: Alignment target for named confidence scales, retention of divergent assessments, and expression of assertion withdrawal and validity windows.
Alignment target for the handling markings carried on report renditions and notification-content drafts, including marking placement requirements.
Alignment target for expressing coverage and completeness as quality measurements against named metrics. It is a Working Group Note, so this is an expression alignment and not a conformance claim.

owner_package_requirements: Name a single accountable owner for the report register, the versioned propagation rule sets, the declared confidence scale and the published minimum disclosure set before any report may be issued.
Declare the identifier authority for report instances, conclusion anchors, evidence items and renditions, and state which tier of the identity priority it occupies.
Bind this reporting surface to a host subject model and to a snapshot source of record; adoption without both bindings is not permitted because no report could then be reproducible.

Name the external models that own approval, remediation, notification delivery, audit records, retention execution and access grants, so that every non-authorising declaration resolves to a real owner.
Publish the staleness threshold and the cycle cut rule with versions, since conclusions depend on both and neither has a universal default.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Allocate report, conclusion-anchor, evidence-item and rendition identifiers within a Dimension-controlled namespace segment (for example an authority-scoped path such as <dimension>/xct/dep/report/...) that remains stable across storage migration and interface change. Never derive an identifier from a file path, storage collection, serialization format, snapshot digest or issue date. Never reuse an identifier after supersession or tombstoning. Where an external standard already governs an entity, keep that governed identifier as the primary reference and record any local identifier as an alias, not a replacement.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 for WM-XCT-037 at nav path NAV.XCT.DEP with domain tag XCT.DEP
The adopting Dimension's register of versioned propagation rule sets, edge-type filters, staleness thresholds and cycle cut rules
The adopting Dimension's register of declared confidence scales and disclosure methods
The adopting Dimension's published minimum disclosure set that gates release from draft

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the abstract report record: ordered conclusion set with anchors, evidence register, path set, excluded-edge register, degradation register and disclosure block. JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and database representations are projections and never the source of truth.
Normalize every timestamp to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z before hashing; do not normalize an offset away or collapse distinct event, observation and issue times into one field.
Sort every collection by stable identifier rather than by insertion or storage order before computing an integrity digest.
Resolve every internal citation to an identifier, never to an array index, line number or document position.
Carry an explicit no-assertion value where a completeness or confidence value is absent; an omitted field is never canonicalised into a positive claim.
patch_rules: A published report revision is immutable. Corrections are issued as a new revision that cites and supersedes the prior one; the prior content is never rewritten.
Draft revisions may be patched in place only while status is draft and no external citation to them exists.
Any patch that changes a conclusion, path set, exclusion, degradation entry, evidence citation or disclosure value forces a new revision and a full recomputation of the disclosure block.
Every patch records the snapshot binding and the propagation rule set version it was computed against, so that a later reader can tell an input change from an analysis change.
Marking an evidence item as withdrawn is applied as a patch to the evidence register and mandatorily triggers a confidence and completeness downgrade in the affected revision's successor.
compatibility_rules: Adding a new report kind, a new optional disclosure field or a new degradation condition type is backward compatible; removing or narrowing a disclosure field is a breaking change.
Changing a propagation rule set version is a breaking analytical change: prior reports remain valid against the rule version they cite and must never be silently re-interpreted under a newer version.
Changing the confidence scale definition invalidates cross-revision comparison of confidence values unless a recorded mapping exists between the scales.
External vocabulary alignments may be extended freely, but conformance to an external standard is claimed only where mapping evidence is recorded in this model.
Consumers must tolerate unknown optional fields and must not treat an unrecognised degradation condition type as absence of degradation.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for reports in the adopting Dimension.
Governed global identifier or IRI where a registry, standard or namespace authority already governs the report or the cited evidence item.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension where neither of the preceding exists.
A date, title, storage path, snapshot digest or revision digest is never an identifier; a digest corroborates integrity only, and an issue date is an attribute.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; a value lacking seconds or lacking an offset is invalid and must be rejected rather than assumed to be UTC. Where they differ, record graph event time (when the dependency fact became true), observation or ingestion time (when the snapshot captured it) and report issue time as separate fields, and never overwrite an earlier observation time with a later ingestion time. Evidence observation time and evidence assertion time are likewise held separately, because staleness is computed against the earlier of the two.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Report artifacts are serial: each is addressed by its report identifier plus a monotonically increasing integer revision. Renditions of one revision share that revision number and add a rendition discriminator, plus a language variant tag where more than one human-readable variant exists. Revision numbers are never reused, never renumbered after supersession, and never encode a date; a gap in the sequence is itself information and must not be closed by renumbering.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every issued revision carries a digest over its canonical form, together with the bound snapshot digest and the version of every propagation rule set, staleness threshold and cycle cut rule applied. A rendition is valid only while its digest chain resolves to the same revision; a broken chain marks the rendition unusable and requires an explicit regeneration or a new revision, never a silent rewrite. Tombstoned revisions retain their digest so that historical citations can still be checked against what was actually issued.

policies: No report may leave draft status without a complete minimum disclosure set: snapshot binding and digest, propagation rule set version, excluded-edge register, degradation register reference, completeness assertion, coverage statement, and a confidence value with its named scale.

A report states conclusions and their confidence. It never records an approval, dispatches a notification, applies or verifies a mitigation, or asserts that an operation has been completed; each such act is declared as belonging to a named external model.

Contradictory and stale evidence is disclosed with both sides retained. A report may state a preferred reading with an explicit rationale but must never delete, overwrite or silently rank away the assertion it did not prefer.
Absence of evidence is reported as an explicit no-assertion and never as a negative finding; unreached territory is never presented as unaffected territory.

A human-readable rendition may summarise but may not drop any disclosure whose loss would change the safe reading of a conclusion, and every conclusion it asserts must carry the anchor of its machine-readable counterpart.
A cycle cut, a depth bound and an excluded edge are reporting devices. None of them may be written back to the dependency graph or presented as an assertion about the real system.

read: Any principal holding read scope on the host subject and on the bound snapshot may resolve a report's conclusions, evidence citations, path set, registers and disclosures; resolution of a cited external entity remains governed by the model that owns it.
Reading a superseded revision must return its supersession pointer alongside its content, so that a stale citation is visibly stale.
Coverage, completeness and degradation disclosures are never withheld from a principal permitted to read the conclusions they qualify.
Reading a tombstoned revision returns the retained tombstone fields and the disposition reason rather than a bare not-found response.
create: A report instance is created only after a snapshot binding, a frozen scenario declaration and a named propagation rule set version are all in place.
Creation mints a report identifier under the declared identity priority and opens the instance at revision one in draft status.
Evidence register entries are created by citation: an entry must resolve to an existing item in its owning source and must not restate or fork that item's content.
Renditions are created only for a revision that has a conformance verdict against the minimum disclosure set.
update: Draft revisions may be updated in place while uncited; published revisions are changed only by issuing a superseding revision.

Any update to scenario, snapshot binding, propagation rule version, exclusion register, degradation register or evidence register invalidates the existing disclosure block and requires recomputation before re-publication.
Supersession updates only the prior revision's status pointer; its conclusions, registers and digest are never rewritten.
Marking a cited evidence item as withdrawn updates the register entry and mandatorily downgrades the confidence and completeness disclosures that depended on it.
delete: Published report revisions are never deleted in place. They are tombstoned with a retained report identifier, kind, revision number, issue time, revision digest, supersession pointer and disposition reason, so that prior citations continue to resolve to a truthful record of what existed.

Retention periods, legal-hold overrides, disposition scheduling and physical erasure are executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention and disposition model and its storage layer. This model owns only the tombstone contract, the minimum retained field set and the requirement that a disposition be recorded; it does not own or perform deletion.
Draft revisions that were never cited externally may be hard-deleted; once cited, they follow the tombstone rule.

Deletion or redaction of a cited evidence item is performed by the model that owns that evidence. This model records the resulting evidence-withdrawal marker, downgrades the affected disclosures and, where the redaction changes a conclusion, requires a superseding revision rather than an in-place edit.
Every tombstone and every hard deletion of a draft emits a record to the referenced audit and event-record model, which owns that record's storage and retention.

roles.name: Report Owner
responsibilities: Accountable for the report register, the identifier authority and the published minimum disclosure set
Approves the tombstone and disposition contract with the records-retention model
Ensures every non-authorising declaration resolves to a currently valid external owner

roles.name: Analysis Author
responsibilities: Declares and freezes the scenario, binds the snapshot and selects the propagation rule set version
Composes conclusions and cites evidence for each
Holds no approval authority and records no decision outcome

roles.name: Disclosure Reviewer
responsibilities: Verifies the confidence, completeness, coverage and degradation disclosures before a revision leaves draft
Checks that confidence values are consistent with the completeness and evidence they summarise
Returns a conformance verdict; does not gate or publish

roles.name: Rule-Set Steward
responsibilities: Maintains and versions propagation rules, edge-type filters, depth bounds, staleness thresholds and cycle cut rules
Publishes each version so that prior reports remain interpretable against the version they cite
Records the breaking-change implications of any rule version change

roles.name: Rendition Editor
responsibilities: Produces the human-readable rendition anchored to the machine-readable conclusion identifiers
Attests rendition equivalence and confirms no non-droppable disclosure was lost
Applies the handling marking inherited from the most restrictive incorporated evidence

roles.name: Change Decision Authority (external, referenced only)
responsibilities: Receives readiness and impact reports as inputs and owns the approval decision
Recorded in this model solely as an addressed role reference on the non-authorising declaration
Its decisions are stored in the change approval model, never in a report record

access.default_rule: A report revision is readable by principals holding read scope on the host subject and on the bound snapshot. Where evidence items carry handling markings, the most restrictive marking among all incorporated evidence governs the whole revision and both of its renditions; the marking is displayed on the rendition itself and constrains onward sharing.
exceptions: A notification-content draft may be readable by a wider audience than its evidence register. In that case the register is referenced but not disclosed, and the draft must state that a restricted evidence set exists rather than implying the conclusions are unsupported.

Under legal hold or embargo a revision may be sealed so that only its identifier, kind, revision number and issue time are readable; the seal is applied and lifted by the referenced access and retention models.

Emergency time-boxed read scope on a change-readiness report may be granted to incident responders; the grant, its expiry and its revocation are issued and recorded by the adopting Dimension's access model, not by this model.
A superseded revision may retain broader read scope than its successor where prior recipients must be able to verify what they were originally told.
audit_requirements: Issuance, supersession, tombstoning, evidence withdrawal and disclosure recomputation must each emit a record to the adopting Dimension's audit and event-record model. This model specifies the required content of those records and never stores, protects or evaluates the audit trail itself.
Read of a sealed revision or of a restricted evidence register must be recorded by the referenced access and audit models.
Rendition equivalence attestations must be recorded with the attesting role and time, and made resolvable from both renditions.
Retention, protection and evaluation of all such records are governed entirely by the referenced audit model's policy, not by this model.

required_fields: Referenced models for approval, remediation, notification delivery, audit, retention and access
read_order: AGENTS.md first: resolve Name, Type and the four mandatory URLs before taking any other action.
Specification URL: the format-neutral report contract in this model, including bundles, layers, findings and the mandatory disclosure obligations.
Storage type URL: how report revisions, registers and renditions are persisted in this deployment, remembering that the storage form is a projection and not the semantics.
Interface URL: how to read and create report records, and confirmation that no approval, execution, remediation or delivery operation is exposed by this model.
Processes URL: the ordered procedures for binding a snapshot, declaring a scenario, traversing, detecting degradation, computing disclosures, composing, validating, rendering and superseding.
Referenced-model entries last: resolve the owners of approval, remediation, notification delivery, audit, retention and access before attempting any act this model explicitly does not perform.

coverage.claim: This deliverable covers the bounded impact-and-readiness reporting surface of WM-XCT-037 only: the five report kinds, the analysis frame each must declare, mandatory evidence and disclosure obligations, degraded-graph handling and dual-rendition traceability. Its structure is grounded in dependency, provenance, quality and advisory standards from nine independent organisations, and it deliberately declines authority over approval, execution, remediation, delivery, audit storage and deletion execution. It does not cover typed edge assertion, graph storage, scoring or the non-reporting areas of this mixin, and it makes no claim of completeness beyond the reporting surface.

checklist.notes: Report instance identity, revision, conclusion anchors, evidence item identifiers and rendition identifiers are defined, with an identity priority whose first tier is the authoritative master-system identifier and an explicit prohibition on dates, digests and storage paths as identifiers.

Draft, interim and final release status, supersession pointers, withdrawal markers and the tombstone contract cover this model's own records. The lifecycle of the analysed change itself is explicitly out of scope and referenced to the change approval model.

Traversal filters, propagation rule mappings, path edge steps, exclusion reasons and alternative satisfier sets are defined. Edge type definitions, dependency strengths and edge assertion lifecycle are consumed through the COMPOSE link and are not restated.

Graph event time, snapshot observation or ingestion time, evidence observation and assertion time, and report issue time are separate fields under an RFC 3339 rule requiring seconds and an explicit offset. Validity horizons and staleness thresholds are declared, not defaulted.

The evidence register records generating activity, derivation source, responsible agent and observation time, aligned to PROV-O starting-point terms, and distinguishes observation from third-party assertion and inference.

Six roles are defined with the decision authority marked external. Boundary notes and composition links name the owning model for approval, remediation, delivery, audit, retention, access, inventory and scoring.

A disclosure-contract validation function returns an itemised conformance verdict, and confidence-consistency rules cap confidence against completeness and evidence conditions. Enforcement of the verdict is explicitly left to the adopting Dimension.

Default read rule with most-restrictive marking inheritance, four scopes, four exception cases including seals and time-boxed emergency access, and audit content requirements. Grant and revocation execution belongs to the referenced access model.

Published revisions are tombstoned with a defined minimum retained field set; retention periods, legal holds and physical erasure are executed by the referenced records-retention model and its storage layer. This model owns only the tombstone contract and the requirement that a disposition be recorded.

Eight ALIGN links to SPDX, ECMA-424/CycloneDX, CSAF, OpenVEX, SARIF, STIX, PROV-O and DQV, each stated as alignment rather than conformance, with six substantive conflicts recorded rather than smoothed over.
Five report kinds with mandatory content cores, exclusion reason codes, evidence kinds, impact classes and dependency strength classes are all closed-vocabulary and versioned.

Confidence values require a named scale and coverage is expressed as a measurement against a named metric. No specific scoring or coverage algorithm is mandated; the model requires only that the method be declared and versioned.
Every conclusion carries resolvable evidence citations plus completeness, coverage and confidence values, and a minimum disclosure set gates release from draft.

Contradictions with both sides retained, staleness thresholds, unresolvable endpoints, cycle detection with disclosed cut points, alternative satisfiers without selection, and partial coverage are all mandatory disclosures with a dedicated register artifact.
A non-authorising declaration is a required field on every rendition, naming each non-performed act and its owning model. No function has an approval, dispatch, apply or complete effect.

Integrity digests and digest chains are specified, but signing, key management, signature verification and tamper-evidence for report revisions are not modelled here and would need a cryptographic assurance model or a Dimension-level extension.

Notification-content drafts and evidence registers may embed personal data. Minimisation, lawful basis, data-subject rights and cross-border transfer are not constrained by this model and are left to the adopting Dimension's privacy model.

Dependency and impact relations here are topological rather than geographic. Where physical or jurisdictional location affects an impact conclusion it enters as an attribute of a referenced element, not as a construct of this surface.

known_omissions: No quantitative impact scoring, severity algorithm or business-criticality weighting is specified; scores enter by reference from a risk or severity model with their scoring system named.
Cost, effort, resourcing and scheduling estimation for a proposed change are absent.
Graph storage, indexing, query language and traversal performance characteristics are deliberately excluded as projection concerns.
Human and organisational readiness - training, staffing, stakeholder communications planning - is not covered; change-readiness here is technical dependency readiness only.
No normative algorithm is fixed for cycle cutting, coverage measurement or confidence derivation; the model requires that each method be declared and versioned, not that a particular method be used.
Live simulation or what-if execution against a running environment is out of scope; scenarios remain declarative.
Cross-organisation report exchange profiles, including transport bindings and signature formats, are not specified.
Aggregation of many reports into a portfolio or programme-level view is not modelled and may require a separate aggregation surface.
Machine-learning or heuristic inference of missing edges is not addressed; any such inference would have to enter as an evidence item of kind inference with its own confidence.
conflicts: SPDX 3.0.1 expresses completeness per relationship, while ECMA-424 / CycloneDX expresses it per composition scope. A report mixing both must state which granularity each completeness claim uses; the two are not interchangeable and no lossless merge is claimed.

CSAF 2.0 and OpenVEX define overlapping but non-identical status and justification vocabularies. Mapping between them loses information in at least one direction, so no lossless bidirectional mapping is asserted.

SARIF baselineState describes result drift between runs, whereas STIX revoked and valid_until describe withdrawal and expiry of an assertion. Using either alone under-reports staleness, so this model requires both an age-based staleness marker and a withdrawal marker.

Debian-style alternatives expressed with a vertical bar and virtual capabilities expressed through Provides encode choice inside the dependency declaration, whereas SPDX and CycloneDX dependency graphs commonly record already-resolved edges. A report converting between these can silently lose the alternative set, which is why alternative satisfiers are a mandatory degradation disclosure.

STIX confidence scales are enumerated but not universal. A numeric confidence value copied between scales without naming the scale is not interoperable, so the scale reference is required alongside every value.
W3C DQV is a Working Group Note rather than a Recommendation, so its use here is an expression alignment for quality measurement and explicitly not a conformance claim.

NIST treats impact analysis as an analytical act distinct from configuration change control, whereas several commercial change-management tools merge assessment and approval into one record. This model follows the standards-led separation and will therefore not map cleanly onto tools that combine them.
regional_assumptions: No jurisdiction-specific breach, outage or incident notification duty is modelled. A notification-content draft is a draft whose legal sufficiency and timing must be assessed by the adopting Dimension's regulatory model.

TLP 2.0 is assumed as the handling-marking vocabulary. Dimensions operating under a mandated national or sectoral marking scheme must map to it and record the mapping rather than substituting silently.
Retention periods and legal-hold semantics are left entirely to the adopting Dimension because statutory minimums differ by jurisdiction and sector.
The language of a human-readable rendition is a Dimension choice; where multiple language variants exist, the equivalence attestation must cover each variant separately.
Working-day, business-hour and freeze-window conventions that may bear on readiness criteria are not encoded here and must come from the adopting Dimension's calendar or change model.
adversarial_checks: Does any bundle, layer, finding or function grant approval, execution, remediation, delivery or audit-trail authority? Each was re-read against the boundary notes and the relation ledger. Approval, execution, remediation, delivery, audit storage, retention execution and access grants appear only as REFERENCE targets, out-of-scope entries and named owners on the non-authorising declaration. No function effect performs any of them, and the validation function explicitly returns a verdict without enforcing it.

Could a report be published that conceals its own blind spots? The minimum disclosure set makes excluded edges, cut cycles, unknown endpoints, contradictions, stale assertions and coverage measurement mandatory before a revision leaves draft. Absence of a value canonicalises to explicit no-assertion rather than to complete, and unreached territory may not be presented as unaffected.

Could the human-readable rendition assert something the machine-readable rendition does not? Both share the revision digest and the conclusion anchors, an equivalence attestation is required, and a human-readable claim without an anchor is by rule not a conclusion of record. A drifting rendition breaks the digest chain and is marked unusable rather than silently regenerated.

Does this surface re-define typed edge semantics owned by the adjacent graph area? Edge types, dependency strengths and edge assertion lifecycle are consumed through the COMPOSE link. Only traversal filters, propagation mappings and reporting obligations are defined locally, and cycle cuts, bounds and exclusions are explicitly barred from being written back to the graph.

Would re-analysis against a newer snapshot silently overwrite an earlier conclusion? No. Snapshot binding is frozen per revision, a different snapshot forces a new revision with a supersedes pointer, and the prior revision's content and digest are never rewritten.

Is a digest or a date being used as an identifier anywhere? Explicitly prohibited in identity_priority and in the serial naming rule; digests corroborate integrity only and issue dates are attributes. Every local ID was checked for date-like components.

Does the evidence register drift into being an audit trail? It is scoped to a single report revision and defined as a citation list. A dedicated question, a boundary note and the audit requirements all state that recording, retaining, protecting and evaluating event records belongs to the referenced audit model, to which this model only emits required content.

Could a contradiction be resolved silently to make a report look cleaner? The policy retains both assertions, permits a preferred reading only with an explicit stated rationale, and mandates a confidence downgrade for dependent conclusions.
